note: Start with a C5/C6 root split to create two manageable, high-value blend branches.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) Establish a root split between C5-and-lighter and C6-and-heavier. (2) Build a compact blend-oriented tree, then purify only the highest-value cuts where economics justify it. (3) Tune stages/reflux and prune weak branches.
Initial root at 50 stages, R=B=3, 10% pressure drop. C5 blend is worth ~$618M/yr and C6 paraffin blend ~$1.15bn/yr, so avoid full component-by-component separation initially.

note: Build a sharpened blend-oriented tree, including the three valuable heavy products, to get a strong full-plant baseline.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) Sharpen the C5/C6 root split. (2) Produce C3, C4, C5, C6-paraffin and C6-naphthene blends plus pure C7-C9 products in one seven-column tree. (3) Inspect recoveries/purities, then tune only limiting columns and prune uneconomic branches.
Initial root at 50 stages R=B=3 was too sloppy: substantial C5 entered B. Raising root to 60 stages R=B=6 should protect blend purities/recoveries. The blend tree avoids expensive separation of close-boiling isomers. Heavy branch uses sequential C7, C8, C9 splits; all three are valuable pure products.

note: Add finishing columns for the four high-value blend products, sharpen the C3/C4 cut, and prune the currently uneconomic heavy branch.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) Keep the sharp C5/C6 root split. (2) Convert the existing tree into four profitable blend outlets (C3, C4, C5, C6 paraffin) by adding only the necessary finishing splits. (3) Prune the uneconomic heavy-pure branch, inspect revenues, then reduce root/energy costs.
The prior seven-column tree earned nothing because mixed adjacent blends are worthless. TB is already ~99% C4+C5, so one column there can yield both blends. BT needs a C5/C6 split. TT needs a sharper C3/C4 cut; TTT then removes ethane from the C3 blend. Heavy C7-C9 columns are pruned for now because their stranded revenue did not justify their cost.

note: Sharpen the C3/C4, C4/C5 and two C5/C6 cuts to recover the large C4 and C6 blend revenues currently just below specification.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) Keep the sharp C5/C6 root split. (2) Convert the existing tree into four profitable blend outlets (C3, C4, C5, C6 paraffin) by adding only the necessary finishing splits. (3) Prune the uneconomic heavy-pure branch, inspect revenues, then reduce root/energy costs.
Current turn: sharpen the four cuts that strand C4 and C6 product. C3 and C5 already sell. TTB has 12% C3 contamination, TBT has 15% C5 contamination, and BTB is only 87% C6 paraffin; more duty at TT, TB, B and BT should recover roughly $770M/yr. Once purity is achieved, reduce the very expensive root and avoid further low-value branches.

note: Prune the uneconomic light branch and recover both high-value C5 and C6 blends in a compact four-column tree.
notebook:
PLAN: (1) Retain the sharp C5/C6 root split. (2) Concentrate on the two valuable C5 and C6 blend products with a compact root-B-BT-BTT tree. (3) Prune all light and heavy pure-product branches, establish positive reward, then cut column duties and pressures.
The seven-column tree costs $895M and strands most product. C5 and C6 blends are worth about $950M combined, while C3/C4 recovery adds too many columns. Agent-3 shows BT at 90/8 produces a saleable C6 blend. I am pruning T, raising BT to 80/8, and adding BTT to recover the C5-rich tops as C5 blend. Next optimize costs rather than purity beyond 95%.

note: Adopt the proven R43 baseline immediately, then improve its economics from a positive-reward design.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt agent-3's proven four-column C6 blend design. (2) Recover the large C5-rich stream economically. (3) Reduce pressure and duties while retaining both blend products. Agent-3's R43 earns $917M from two C6 blend cuts for $759M cost; my sharper columns instead destroyed both products. Copy this exact valid baseline before experimenting.

note: Adopt R52 and strengthen its small C5 finishing column, aiming to recover much of the N-pentane currently lost to the unsold bottoms.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Adopt agent-3's five-column R52 design with its C5 finisher. (2) Strengthen only that small finisher to recover more of the 60 mol/s N-pentane currently lost to its bottoms. (3) Then reduce pressure and duties on the expensive full-feed columns while retaining blend specifications. R52 earns 0.517; its BTTT top is already 98% C5 but captures only about 100 of 160 mol/s C5. A modest 45-stage, 5/5 finisher should add saleable C5 for little cost.

note: Restore the cheaper C5 finisher and reduce the dominant B-column size and duty, testing whether blend purity and recovery are preserved.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Use the proven five-column R52 blend tree. (2) Restore its cheaper C5 finisher. (3) Reduce the expensive B-column duty while checking both C6 blend outlets remain on specification; then optimize the root similarly. R52 scores 0.517. The 45/5 finisher added only $2.9M revenue for $4.6M cost, so it is counterproductive. Root+B cost $602M/yr and dominate economics. Current test: B 55/4.5/4.5 instead of 70/6/6, which should save substantially if its N-hexane/MCP split remains adequate.

note: Restore R52 and test a cheaper root at the same C5/C6 separation; the root is the largest single cost and modest stage/reflux reductions may preserve all blend revenue.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Restore proven R52 (0.517). (2) Reduce dominant full-feed root cost first, without moving its C5/C6 cut. (3) If successful, tune B and BT only while preserving both C6 blend outlets; do not repeat the failed B 55/4.5 test. R52 revenue/cost are $1005.9M/$779.0M. Root alone costs $331.6M, so 50 stages and ratios 4.0 are the highest-value test. The B reduction failed because BTB fell to 93% C6 and lost $617.8M revenue. BTTT finisher at 35/4 is optimal versus 45/5. Unsold light and BB streams are too expensive to recover.

note: Test the midpoint between R52's root and the failed cheap root; this may retain blend specifications while saving roughly $30M/yr.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Restore proven R52 (0.517). (2) Test an intermediate 55/4.5 root after 50/4 lost both C6 blend outlets. (3) If revenue is preserved, tune B/BT conservatively; otherwise restore R52 and seek a different saving. R52 revenue/cost $1005.9M/$779.0M; root $331.6M. The 50/4 root saved $57.9M but lost $273.1M revenue, so 55/4.5 is the logical interpolation. B 55/4.5 failed by dropping BTB below 95% C6; do not repeat. BTTT 35/4 is better than 45/5.

note: Strengthen the small C5/C6 finisher to push BTTB just over the C6 blend threshold while retaining the cheaper root's revenue and savings.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Restore R52-like revenue while retaining the cheaper 55/4.5 root by strengthening only BTTT. (2) If the C6 blend at BTTB is recovered, keep this improved plant and make one conservative economics test. (3) Otherwise restore R52. Current root saves about $29M versus R52 and preserves BTB/C5 revenue, but loses $296M because BTTB is fractionally below 95% C6. R52 at 60/5 gives $1005.9M revenue/$779.0M cost. BTTT 45/5 on R52 cost only about $1.7M extra and scored 0.513, so it is the cheapest targeted fix here. Avoid more heavy/light branches: shown attempts are uneconomic.

note: Test a modest reduction in the second-largest column while restoring R52's proven root and downstream settings; the blend products may tolerate this saving.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Restore R52 exactly and reduce only the expensive B column from 70/6 to 65/5.5, preserving its pressure drop. (2) If both C6 blends and C5 remain saleable, retain the savings and consider one further modest reduction; otherwise restore R52 and finish. Root reductions to 55/4.5 or 57.5/4.75 failed by losing BTTB blend revenue, but B itself has not yet been economically optimized. R52 gives $1005.9M revenue/$779.0M cost, reward 0.517. B costs $269.9M, so a modest duty/size reduction is the clearest remaining targeted saving. Avoid extra heavy/light branches: all shown attempts are uneconomic.

note: Reduce B one further modest step to 60 stages and reflux/boil-up 5.0; the previous reduction preserved all three blend products, so another $15–20M saving may be available.
notebook: PLAN: (1) Restore R52 exactly and reduce only expensive B from 70/6 to 65/5.5: succeeded, reward 0.545, revenue $996.2M/cost $757.3M. (2) Test B at 60/5/5/0.25, the same duty as BT, while watching BTTB's sensitive C6-blend specification. If revenue holds, retain; otherwise revert to the 0.545 design. Root reductions failed; light/heavy expansions and BTTTB finishing are uneconomic. Remaining solves are scarce because changing B re-solves its three descendants.

note: Restore the 0.545 design and make a final low-cost trim of only the small terminal C5 finisher, whose products have some purity margin.
notebook: PLAN: Best is 0.545: R52 root/BT/downstream with B=65/5.5/5.5/.25, revenue $996.2M and cost $757.3M. B=60/5 lost both C6 blends, so restore best. Root reductions and extra light/heavy/finishing columns were uneconomic.
